notes: Ran into the known, unbreakable Piranhas about eight times over four turns, taking net damage each time and binning its own cards, then ran Starlit Knight twice at 0 credits. Economy sat at 0-2 credits for most of the game and there was no plan to find breakers.
Scored steadily from a single-ice remote and used Urtica Cipher as a trap. Some loose credit clicks and thin economy, but it read a passive Runner correctly.
From about turn 6 it clicked for credits four times a turn up to 82 credits, holding 5 cards, never drawing for breakers and almost never running. It just watched the Corp advance and score agendas.
Strong Nico Campaign economy, a good Ansel plus Tranquility Home Grid remote, and fast scoring. The only weakness was leaving R&D behind a single non-ETR Wave, which cost one agenda.

Pressuring R&D every turn through Congratulations! was correct and won the game. But it usually made only one R&D run per turn and spent the rest on single credit clicks and tag removal, even though each extra run paid it a credit.

Kept Méliès in HQ behind an Ansel it could not afford to rez, so it was stolen on turn 3, and later left an ADT and another Méliès in a remote the Runner could get into. Credits stayed at 1-3 for much of the game and it rarely had money to defend.
Efficient: built breakers, kept up R&D pressure and punished the weak Paywall remote for three steals in a row. Only a few low-value credit clicks.

After a lucky triple steal on turn 1 it clicked for credits for about ten turns, up to 48, with a full grip, never drawing or contesting HQ or R&D. It skipped free Archives runs while the Corp discarded every turn and only won late by checking Archives.
Economy fell to 1-3 credits early and never recovered, leaving HQ full of agendas behind one ice, and the Runner took three of them. It played no economy cards and left R&D unprotected on turn 1.
Clean, fast scoring out of one iced remote, with R&D left open early (a slight gamble that paid off). Money was tight but enough.

After two quick scores it left R&D behind a single Ping that the Runner broke for 1 credit, letting it run R&D twice a turn for seven turns, and it never added ice there. Credits sank to 0-3 and Next Big Thing sat unadvanced in a remote until it was stolen.

Reasonable pressure and good steals from HQ, R&D and an open remote. But it repeatedly bounced off a reinstalled Descent without a decoder and ran Ballista short on credits, losing Boi-tatá, while Fencer Fueno drained its economy.

Spent its last credits and clicks trashing a resource while the Runner pressured its agendas, so it ended several turns on 0 credits. Then it installed and advanced Next Big Thing into a remote the Runner had already broken into.
Good use of Red Team for money and well-timed HQ runs with Docklands Pass, two double steals. It ate a couple of Urtica Cipher traps, which is acceptable risk.
Steady multi-server pressure and good steals. It deliberately tanked Karunā damage to steal Yagi-Uda, and once jacked out after taking Anemone damage, wasting that run.
Solid economy, a layered remote, Vertigo slowing the Runner, and steady scoring to the win. HQ and R&D had only one ice each, which leaked a couple of agendas.

Strong early aggression, but once its breakers were gone it spent about ten turns clicking for credits, removing self-inflicted Trickster Taka tags and running only Archives. It did not dig for breakers against a broke Corp until turn 26.
A sensible remote behind Karunā and an Urtica trap won the game. But the Runner took a Yagi-Uda from HQ and two agendas from the remote while the Corp hovered near 0 credits.

Went broke by turn 3 and kept agendas in an HQ behind only Vertigo, which lost Project Ingatan and Megaprix. It recovered with Nico Campaigns and an Ansel/Drafter decoy remote that soaked up the Runner's clicks while it scored elsewhere.
Made one run all game and otherwise clicked for credits up to 42, never contesting a remote where the Corp installed and advanced four agendas over several turns. There was no coherent plan.
